newsitem.title: USA: Brown & WilliamsON throws wrench into talks - reports.
newsitem.headline: Brown & WilliamsON throws wrench into talks - reports.

text.p: Tobacco settlement talks have become bogged down as Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp balked at a proposal concerning regulatory control over nicotine, according to news reports.

In Wednesday's editions, the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal said Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, has apparently broken ranks with other cigarette makers over the issue.
With Brown & Williamson in dispute over the amount of control that should be awarded the Food and Drug Administration over nicotine, talks have broken down, both newspapers said.
B.A.T Chief Executive Martin Broughton is scheduled to arrive in Washington, where the talks are being held, to try to deal with the impasse, the Journal reported.

It is unclear what the ultimate effect could be from Brown & Williamson's position. Some negotiators said it would merely delay a final agreement until next week, while others said it the No. 3 cigarette maker could end up withdrawing from the talks entirely.

Unnamed sources close to the talks told both newspapers that Brown & Williamson was concerned about the effect regulations crafted by the federal government in the United States could have elsewhere around the world.

"B.A.T is having second thoughts about the whole deal, and the (FDA provision) is just a pretext," one source told the Journal. "Because they are a European company, they are concerned that this whole regulatory scheme would set an example and they would be unable to effectively resist regulation in other countries."
